title: Word Ladder
prompt:
A transformation sequence from `beginWord` to `endWord` changes **one letter at a time**, and every intermediate word (and `endWord`) must be in `wordList`. `beginWord` doesn't need to be in the list. Return the number of words in the **shortest** sequence, including both ends, or `0` if none exists.

**Example**: `beginWord = "hit"`, `endWord = "cog"`, `wordList = ["hot","dot","dog","lot","log","cog"]` → `5` (hit → hot → dot → dog → cog).

**Constraints**: all words have the same length (1–10), lowercase; `wordList` has up to 5000 words.
hints: Think of each word as a node. Which words are connected, and what kind of search finds the fewest hops?
Use BFS from `beginWord`, one layer at a time. Words one letter apart are neighbors. Put `wordList` in a `HashSet` for O(1) lookups and return 0 early if `endWord` isn't there.
Generate neighbors instead of comparing all pairs: for each position, try `'a'..'z'`. `if (words.remove(next)) q.offer(next);` both checks membership and marks visited.

solution.explanation: Words are nodes and one-letter changes are edges. BFS visits words in order of distance, so the layer where `endWord` first appears is the shortest ladder, and starting the counter at 1 counts words rather than edges. Removing words from the set when enqueued stops them from being visited again. O(N·L²) time with 26·L candidates per word, each costing O(L) to build and hash; O(N·L) space.
